title: Artaxerxes warns that trusted advisers can lead rulers into innocent bloodshed
speaker: King Artaxerxes (royal letter)
recipient: the satraps, rulers and loyal subjects
note: Gnomic warning in the letter's preamble; the long record ot-esther-v8-11 captures only the decree's provisions.

title: Job's wife urges him to speak to God and die
speaker: Job's wife
note: Her speech begins at 2:9 ('How long will you persist…?'); extend the reference to the whole speech, 2:9–9e.

title: Eliphaz: those who plow wrong and sow it reap pains
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Widen first-pass B10 P01249 (Job 4:8) to 4:8–9: v9 completes the saying. Merge with it; do not add a second record.

title: Job tells his friends that keeping silent would be their wisdom
speaker: Job
note: Outside candidate list (context verse) between 13:4 and recorded 13:6; cf. Proverbs 17:28 (first-pass B12 P01694).

title: Let the faithful hold their way and the clean-handed take courage
speaker: Job
note: 17:9 is a context verse; jussive exhortation that the righteous persevere and resist the lawless, otherwise unrecorded.

title: Job appeals to what travelers have seen
speaker: Job
note: The sentence runs on: the travellers' signs show the wicked are kept for the day of destruction.

title: God humbles the arrogant and saves the one with downcast eyes
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Maxim within Eliphaz's promise (22:21–30); cf. Proverbs 3:34, James 4:6. Borderline: 22:30 is only Study Context.

title: Job rescued the poor and orphan and was eyes to the blind
speaker: Job
note: Includes 29:12, 14–17 beyond the candidates; portrait of righteous conduct like first-pass Job 31 findings (B10 P01315).

title: Elihu calls Job to hear his words and listen to his speech
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: Elihu's opening call to listen; the catalogue records like calls (13:17, 34:16) as Commands.

title: Wrath comes on the ungodly for gifts taken to do injustice
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: Immediately precedes ot-job-v36-19 (36:19–21); bribery maxim, cf. Exodus 23:8 (C0225).

title: God tells Job's friends to bring offerings and seek his prayer
speaker: the Lord
note: The Lord's speech to Eliphaz begins at 42:7 with its reason: you did not speak truly, as Job did.

title: Confess sin to the Lord; let every holy one pray in time
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Between first-pass 31:1–2 and 31:8–9: confession brings forgiveness, so the godly should pray in time (31:6, context verse).

title: The sword the wicked draw against the upright pierces their own heart
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
note: Fills the gap between first-pass 36:9–13 and 36:16–17 in this saying-by-saying psalm; 36:15 is worded as a wish, hence low.

title: The psalmist resolves to guard his tongue when sinners confront him
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Autobiographical resolve long read as counsel on restraint of speech; borderline, like first-pass Greek Psalm 100:2–3.

title: Death shepherds the self-assured into Hades; God redeems the upright
speaker: the sons of Korah (wisdom psalm)
note: Fills the gap between first-pass 48:7–13 and 48:17–21 (extend) in this wisdom psalm.

title: God needs no animal sacrifices; the world and its fullness are his
speaker: God, in Asaph's psalm
note: God's rationale before recorded 49:14–15 (offer praise instead); cf. Acts 17:25 and first-pass Greek Psalm 49:16–21.

title: A call to sound instruments and the new moon trumpet
speaker: the psalmist
note: 80:5–6 ground the trumpet call: 'an ordinance for Israel… a testimony in Joseph' (cf. Numbers 10:10, C0848).

title: Whoever dwells in the Most High's help lodges in God's shelter
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the one who trusts in God
note: No records in Greek Psalm 90; thesis of the trust psalm, like first-pass 124:1–2 (B12 P01626).

title: Happy the one whom the Lord disciplines and teaches from his law
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Unrecorded beatitude; cf. Job 5:17 (ot-job-v5-17) and Proverbs 3:11–12 (X006).

title: A ruler banishes slanderers and the proud and keeps the faithful near
speaker: David
recipient: the reader (a king's vow of conduct)
note: Continues first-pass B12 P01569 (100:2–3) with the king's choice of companions; could instead widen that finding to 100:2–7.

title: The Lord's lasting mercy rests on those who keep his covenant
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Conditional promise: mercy for those who fear him, keep his covenant and remember to do his commandments; 102:17 is context.

title: The Lord sent Moses his servant and Aaron his chosen
speaker: the psalmist, recalling God's commission
topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
note: Retells Exodus 3:10 and 4:14–16; link as Additional Scripture like Acts 7:34–35 (cf. first-pass 104:20–22).

title: The Lord's invitation to sit at his right hand
speaker: the Lord (in David's psalm)
note: The oracle continues in 109:2 with a second imperative: 'Exercise dominion in the midst of your enemies.'

title: The Lord swears: You are a priest for ever after Melchizedek
speaker: the Lord, by oath (in David's psalm)
note: Divine oath appointing a priest; quoted in Hebrews 5:6, 7:17, 7:21, which have only Study Context A101.

title: Great peace belongs to those who love God's law
speaker: the psalmist
note: General maxim like first-pass 118:105 and 118:130; the surrounding first-person lines need nothing.

title: Happy is everyone who fears the Lord and walks in His ways
speaker: the psalmist
note: Widen first-pass B12 P01631 (127:1–3) to 127:4, the beatitude's closing line. Merge with it; do not add a record.

title: The psalmist keeps his soul humble like a weaned child
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Example of humility to imitate, applied to Israel in recorded 130:3; borderline autobiography.

title: David's sons must keep God's covenant to keep the throne
speaker: the Lord, sworn to David (quoted by the psalmist)
note: Same Davidic covenant condition as first-pass B11 P01550 (Greek Psalm 88:31–35); cf. 1 Kings 2:4 and 9:4–5. Link them.

title: Happy the people whose God is the Lord
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Same beatitude as first-pass B11 P01417 (Greek Psalm 32:12); no records in Psalm 143.

title: Do not place your trust in mortal rulers
speaker: the psalmist (Haggai and Zechariah)
note: 145:4 gives the reason and 145:5 the contrasting beatitude: happy is the one whose helper is the God of Jacob.

title: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom
speaker: Solomon, the wisdom teacher
note: Outside candidate list (context verse inside ot-proverbs-v9-8); same maxim as Proverbs 1:7 (first-pass B12 P01663) and Greek Psalm 110:10.

title: Whoever leans on lies shepherds the wind and gathers fruitlessness
speaker: Solomon, the wisdom teacher
note: Outside candidate list; Greek saying inside ot-proverbs-v9-8 (9:7–12), whose title does not capture it.

title: The lament calls the people to return to the Lord
speaker: the lamenter
note: 3:39 asks why the living should grumble over their sin, the premise of the call to return.

title: Do not presume on impunity or on God's mercy while sinning
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Inside ot-sirach-v5-1 (5:1–11), whose title covers only wealth and desire.

title: Do not delay turning to the Lord from day to day
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Inside ot-sirach-v5-1 (5:1–11), whose title covers only wealth and desire.

title: Do not be double-tongued; be firm and let your word be one
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Inside ot-sirach-v5-1 (5:1–11); precedes first-pass B14 P01797 (5:11–13).

summary: Mostly narrative, lament and praise needing nothing; gaps are Sirach 5 sayings hidden in a long record, Psalm 109:4's priestly oath, unrecorded psalm beatitudes and maxims, Job counsel, and reference extensions.
